entries.title: Settings follow you everywhere
items: Your settings for this game now follow you to every device — change the music, sound or narrator on one and they're the same everywhere.
Your phone now has switches for Music, Sound effects, Narrator voice and Vibration — and in Table mode the host can set each sound's volume.
The character picture you choose on the website now appears on your phone, and everyone in the room sees it right away.
The Google sign-in button now shows in the page's language, and tells you if your browser blocked the sign-in window.

entries.title: Clearer picture toggle wording
items: The picture toggle now reads "Use my character's picture instead", so it's clear you can show your character's picture rather than your avatar

entries.title: Your VHub picture on your seat
items: Your seat now shows your own VHub picture — on your phone, in the lobby, on the tiles and in every TV scene.
Tap the new account button at the top right of the first screens to sign in, or to open your VHub profile.
Prefer your character's look? Turn on "Use my character's picture instead" when you join or create a game, or from the menu during a game.
The guided demo shows your VHub picture too, with the same account button and picture switch.

entries.title: Sharper Watch the TV scene
items: On your phone, the scene behind "Watch the TV" now looks sharp instead of breaking up.

entries.title: Music returns under the last words
items: After the town votes, the music slips quietly back in under the last words, right up until the card turns.
In the demo, the guide now points to your phone for the day's first discussion, not the TV.
On the demo page, the questions now rest within the footer picture, which fades in gently.
The "first one out sees everything" badge on the TV now has a bit more room inside.

entries.title: Talk as long as you like
items: By default, the daytime discussion no longer runs on a clock — talk as long as you like and move on once everyone taps Ready. The host can still turn on a time limit.
The rumour's whispers now play correctly — you can hear them under the day music, and they no longer blare too loudly at the wrong moment.
The guided demo keeps you on track at every step — only the highlighted spot responds, so you can't tap anything else or close your card while the narrator is speaking.
In the demo, the Secret actions now open at the right step, so you can see who was killed.
The settings menu (⋯) no longer appears during the demo.

entries.title: A smoother guided demo
items: In the guided demo, only the spot it points to responds to your taps — so you can't close your role card or tap anything else while the narrator is still explaining a step.
The whispers no longer play out loud at the early "rumor going around town" moment.
Secret actions now open at the right step, so you can see who was found killed.
The settings menu (⋯) stays hidden during the demo, so it won't get in your way.

entries.title: Cleaner demo page footer
items: The demo page looks tidier: the "More about Palermo Noir" links now sit together in the footer, and the line above the footer is gone.

entries.title: The accused defends before the vote
items: After the first talk each day, the player with the most accusations — at least two — now gets 30 seconds to answer the town before the vote.
The characters in play now show bigger on the TV, so it's easier to read who's in the game.
In the demo, the guide now chooses two of the Lawyer's five cards for you and explains aloud what each one does.
The demo's guide now follows what your phone has shown you: a killer you already know is suggested first, and anyone you've cleared is never suggested.
Every countdown now ticks through its last five seconds, and no clock sits frozen at zero anymore.
The demo now explains what each notebook pin colour means: red for suspect, grey for unsure, gold for trust.
Starting, restarting or changing your role now stops the running demo cleanly, so you won't hear two games at once, and the 2× speed option is gone.
The Lawyer's briefcase no longer offers the Injunction card when there's no Mayor or Kamikaze for it to work on.
Your notebook no longer records who answered yes to a confirmation, matching what the shared TV shows.
The demo page now carries the site's full footer, with its links and social channels.

entries.title: Whispers after a rumour
items: When a rumour spreads at dawn, you'll now hear hushed whispers drift quietly through the day until night falls.
On the TV, the reveal and verdict now sit neatly centred with a slightly smaller card, and the "first one out sees everything" note now hangs in a tidy badge under the logo.
In the guided demo, only the highlighted spot responds to your taps, and you can't dismiss anything or skip ahead while the narrator is speaking.
The demo now walks you through each secret result on your phone, like a Detective's check or a Seer's look, and points to your phone whenever your private info is shown.
When a player is voted out in the demo, their card now greys out and gets stamped, matching the verdict on the TV, and the old "Out" label is gone.
On a computer, the demo's TV now fills more of the screen, with the TV and phone centred top to bottom.

entries.title: Demo explains Table and Notebook
items: The guided demo now walks you through the Table and your Notebook, switching the phone to each one as it explains it.
In the demo, the card you hold and secret actions now fit their contents, with the picture beside the text on small screens, so cards no longer scroll.
In the demo, a secret action that only shows you something now closes when you let go or the narrator finishes; those with buttons to tap stay open.
In the demo, when it's time to tap or hold something, the phone now switches to your own tab so you can see it.
When you skip a night or the deal, you now hear all five final countdown ticks.
Subtitles now use one consistent style.

entries.title: Role stays out while explained
items: In the guided demo, your role card now stays out while the narrator explains it, instead of slipping back the moment you let go.

entries.title: See what each character does
items: The character cards are back to their normal size, and the one you point at or pick now shows large beside them, with its team, what it does, how it wins and a quick tip. On smaller screens you'll see this in the line below.
We removed the confusing "Behind the scenes" view from the demo.
The talk and vote screens now make clear that the arrows are only accusations and that only the vote decides.
Subtitles now sit over the content at the very bottom and never take more than two lines; longer lines are split to fit.
There's now a short pause between spoken lines that would otherwise run together.
The guide's card no longer has a Back button.

entries.title: Taps stay locked through narration
items: In the demo, your taps stay locked while the narrator introduces the roles, instead of unlocking part-way through.

entries.title: Subtitles for every spoken line
items: See subtitles for every spoken line in the demo, marked as the narrator or your guide.
On a computer, the demo now has a bigger TV, with cards that spotlight each step by dimming the rest.
Bigger role cards, now four across on a computer.

entries.title: A clearer guided demo
items: In the guided demo, your taps now wait while the narrator is speaking, and a note tells you when you can carry on
When roles are dealt in the demo, it no longer runs down the whole clock — it moves on once everyone has their card, and you hear the last few seconds tick
The demo now shows "Step 1 of 2" and "Step 2 of 2" at night, so you know why your phone taps twice
A new demo card explains the phone's tabs, including the table and the notebook, after you've seen your card
The TV no longer shows subtitles during the guided demo
TV screens now fade in each time the demo moves to a new step
Scrollbars now appear in gold

entries.title: Bigger role cards
items: The demo's role cards are now bigger, so you can clearly see the characters.
On a phone, you now see two role cards per row.
The "Back to the demo" button no longer shows twice.

entries.title: Demo kept private for now
items: Improvements and fixes.

entries.title: Demo loads with ad blockers
items: The guided demo against bots now loads even if you use an ad blocker or a privacy browser like Brave — no more getting stuck at 5%.

entries.title: Crisp welcome art on big screens
items: The welcome screen art is now crisp and sharp, even on a big TV.

entries.title: Your demo guide now speaks
items: In the guided demo against the bots, your guide now has a full voice, speaking all of its lines out loud in English and Greek.
Fixed the Detective's English introduction, which repeated "each night".

entries.title: The final sound is in
items: Palermo Noir now plays its final sound throughout — the real music, sound effects and background ambience, with the old placeholder sounds gone.

Voices are now the final recordings, and more moments speak than before: each role is introduced as the cards are dealt, "Dawn is coming" before the first night ends, a call when the town is ready to vote and when voting closes, a reminder to join while you wait in the lobby, and the host's pause and resume.
Each phase now plays a full song that loops — in the lobby, the deal, night, day, voting and the finish — instead of a short repeating clip.

Key moments now play their sound to the end before the game moves on — the sunrise, for one, stays on screen until its sound finishes — and the winners' theme plays in full at the end instead of being cut off.

entries.title: Lawyer's powers open smoothly
items: The Lawyer's powers now open with a smooth animation — the form grows and fades in under the card, and closes a touch faster, instead of snapping open.

entries.title: New seafront welcome screen
items: The welcome screen now shows new seafront artwork, sized to look right on both your phone and a shared TV.

entries.title: Demo loads reliably
items: The demo now opens as soon as it's ready, instead of getting stuck on the welcome screen.

entries.title: The guided demo is live
items: Play a whole game of Palermo Noir in your browser, alone at a table of bots, with nothing to install and no account.
Pick one of the 14 roles or Surprise me, a table of 6, 8 or 10, English or Greek, and the short demo (about six minutes) or a full game (about fifteen).
A guide stops the game at each new moment to show you what to tap, and why; Chapters, Back, 2× speed and Behind the scenes help you follow it.
